correctness.rationale: A transpose-fixed point in realization of the symmetric rook-board complex has equal weights on each diagonal singleton or off-diagonal two-square orbit. Such an orbit is an admissible face precisely when its support (one graph vertex or one graph edge) is disjoint from others. Thus the geometric fixed set is PL-homeomorphic to the matching/monomer support simplicial complex L(G). The union U of closed singleton stars is contractible: every finite star intersection is a cone on the face of corresponding singleton vertices and the cover nerve is the full simplex. A face omitted from U selects graph edges only and covers all graph vertices, hence is exactly a perfect matching. Odd n has no such faces and L(G) is contractible. Even n=2k attaches p(G) disjoint (k−1)-simplices along all their boundaries into U; quotienting the contractible CW subcomplex yields a wedge of p(G) S^{k−1}, including n=2 (p+1 components), p=0. Relative integral chain group on oriented perfect matching facets yields signed Aut(G) permutation lattice; full K_2k stabilizer is S2 wr S_k with sign of block permutation only. Own separate small-graph enumeration and GF2 homology checks corroborate six full/nonfull graph examples, not used to infer all graphs or integer torsion-freeness.
